newsitem.title: USA: U.S. said expected to delay next Croatia loan.
newsitem.headline: U.S. said expected to delay next Croatia loan.

text.p: The United States expects to seek to delay a $30 million World Bank loan to Croatia because Zagreb has not followed through with commitments under the Dayton peace accord, a U.S. official said on Monday.
"I believe our intention is to seek to delay that loan for some significant period of time," the official, who spoke on condition of anonymity, told Reuters.

The United States has been reviewing all international financial assistance to Croatia more rigorously since Secretary of State Madeleine Albright announced last month that Washington was serious about making aid conditional on compliance with the 1995 Dayton peace accords that ended the Bosnia war and other demands.

Despite its much publicized threats, the United States decided earlier this month to support a $13 million loan to Croatia from the International Finance Corporation, the private sector arm of the World Bank.

Officials said this was because Croatian President Franjo Tudjman had taken actions that met demands set down by Albright. This included his decision to open the long-closed bridge at Brcko between Croatia and Bosnia, his support for a strengthened Croat-Muslim federation in Bosnia, and ordering the arrest of several people suspected of brutalizing Serbs who tried to return to their pre-war homes in Croatia.

But the official said on Monday that Washington would seek to hold up the $30 million loan that is to be approved later this month because Tudjman's "has not folowed through on some of his commitments, including not taking the necessary steps on war criminals."
